claims.text: Base HfZrTi HEA has limited ductility and toughness due to its phase structure and elemental interactions.
Controlled low-concentration interstitial oxygen addition will improve the tensile ductility of HfZrTi HEA.
Controlled low-concentration interstitial oxygen addition will improve the toughness of HfZrTi HEA.
Oxygen can be incorporated uniformly as an interstitial during HfZrTi alloy processing without extensive phase instability.
Interstitial oxygen addition forms oxygen-induced interstitial complexes in the BCC HfZrTi matrix.
Interstitial oxygen addition may form fine oxygen-stabilized precipitates in the BCC HfZrTi matrix.
Oxygen-induced complexes or precipitates ease dislocation transmission.
Oxygen-induced complexes or precipitates delay crack initiation.
Interstitial oxygen locally alters bonding in the HfZrTi lattice.
Interstitial oxygen induces slight local lattice distortions in HfZrTi.
Oxygen-induced bonding changes and lattice distortions promote favorable precipitate morphologies or ordered complexes.
The proposed precipitate morphologies or ordered complexes reduce dislocation pinning.
Reduced dislocation pinning eases dislocation passage and delays stress concentration.
Oxygen-doped HfZrTi will retain overall BCC phase stability within the beneficial oxygen range.
The magnitude of improvement in oxygen-doped HfZrTi is expected to follow trends observed in related Hf-containing systems.
Excess oxygen may form brittle oxide phases.
Excess oxygen may destabilize the BCC phase.
The beneficial effect of oxygen occurs only within a narrow interstitial oxygen concentration window.
